I or T: A2 [ I or T ] to reach, or cause something to reach, the temperature at which a liquid starts to turn into a gas
B1 [ I or T ] to heat a container, especially one used for cooking, until the liquid in it starts to turn into a gas
T: B1 [ T ] to cook food by putting it in water that is boiling

NONE: › If a container or food boils dry, all the liquid in the container in which the food was cooking turns to gas.
煮乾，燒乾
T: › [ T ] to wash clothes in a container of very hot water

I usually continuous: › [ I usually continuous ] informal to be extremely angry

C: › [ C ] a painful swelling on the skin that is filled with pus (= thick, yellow liquid)

S: › [ S ] the act of washing or cooking something in very hot water

example: Liquid nitrogen boils at a very low temperature.
液態氮在很低的溫度下就會達到沸點。
She scalded herself on some boiling water.
她被開水燙傷了。
If you give water to a small baby to drink, you have to boil it first.
如果你餵嬰兒喝水，必須先把水燒開。
The pan's boiling.
鍋燒開了。
mainly UK Could you boil the kettle for me?
你能替我燒壺水嗎？
I've boiled some potatoes for dinner.
晚飯我煮了些馬鈴薯。
boiled carrots
煮熟的胡蘿蔔
He was boiling with rage.
他怒不可遏。
UK Bring the water to the boil, then add the pasta.
先把水燒開，再加入義大利麵。
US Bring the water to a boil, then add the pasta.
先把水燒開，再加入義大利麵。
Let the liquid come to a/the boil and then reduce the heat.
先將湯汁煮沸，然後關小火。

NONE: › to heat a liquid or food so that part of it is turned into gas and its amount is reduced, or to be reduced in this way
（使）煮濃；（使）熬濃
› to reduce information, usually so that it contains only its most important parts
濃縮，簡化

example: He had boiled down a lengthy report to just a few paragraphs.
他已將大篇幅的報告濃縮成了只有幾段。

NONE: › When a liquid boils away, it all turns into a gas so that none of it is left in liquid form.
（液體）汽化，煮乾
› If a situation or problem boils down to something, that is the main reason for it.
（形勢或問題）主要原因在於，歸結為

example: The problem boils down to one thing - lack of money.
問題歸結為一點——缺錢。

NONE: › If a difficult situation or negative emotion boils over, it cannot be controlled any more and people start to argue or fight.
（形勢或負面情緒）失去控制，爆發
› If a liquid that is being heated boils over, it rises up and flows over the edge of the pan.
（液體）沸溢，煮溢
› If a pan boils over, the liquid in it rises up and flows over the edge.
（容器）沸溢

example: Take the milk off the heat before it boils over.
趁牛奶還沒有煮沸溢出，把它從火上拿下來。
That saucepan is boiling over.
鍋裡的東西煮得溢出來了。

NONE: › to heat up liquid or food in a pan until it boils
燒開，煮沸

example: Could you boil some water up for me?
你能為我燒點水嗎？

NONE: › If a bad emotion boils up, it becomes very strong and difficult to control.
（負面情緒）難以控制

example: Anger suddenly boiled up in him.
他突然怒火中燒。

NONE: A2 (of food) cooked in water that is boiling
水煮的

example: a hard-boiled/soft-boiled egg (= one boiled for a long/short time)
煮得很老／嫩的雞蛋

NONE: › a hard, often brightly coloured sweet
硬糖
› a device that heats water, especially to provide heating and hot water in a house
（尤指房子內供暖和供應熱水的）鍋爐
› the part of a steam engine where water is heated to provide power
（蒸汽機的）汽鍋
› a room in a building or on a ship where the boiler is
鍋爐間，鍋爐房
› a room in which people work very hard to sell products by phone
（透過電話銷售物品的）電話交易所
› a piece of clothing that covers both the upper and lower parts of the body and is worn especially over other clothes to protect them
（做髒活兒的）連衫褲工作服

U: › text that can be copied and used in legal documents or in computer programs, with only very small changes
（在法律文件或者電腦程式中略微修改即可使用的）文件樣板，文件範例
› a way of writing or thinking that is not special and does not show any imagination

example: The lyrics are boilerplate and uninspiring.
歌詞是一派陳詞濫調，單調乏味。

NONE: B2 very hot
極熱的；炎熱的

example: I wish I'd worn something cooler - I'm boiling.
要是穿涼快點兒多好——我熱死了。
We don't usually have such boiling hot weather.
我們這兒的天氣通常沒有這麽熱。

S or C: › [ S or C ] The boiling point of a liquid is the temperature at which it becomes a gas.

S: › [ S ] the point when a situation is about to get out of control and become violent
› [ S ] the stage at which someone is about to become very angry

example: UK The situation in the inner city was reaching/at boiling point, so the police were out in force.
內城的形勢快要失控了，所以員警都全副武裝出動了。
US The situation in the inner city was reaching/at the boiling point, so the police were out in force.
內城的形勢快要失控了，所以員警都全副武裝出動了。

NONE: › noisy, energetic, and rough
喧閙的；精力旺盛的

example: a boisterous game
激烈的遊戲
